Issue: #238 (fixes it). Follow-up filed: #239.

One commit. Message (keep the trailer):
```
R1 238: Round Invitations reach the Email queue, on the date the cadence names

A Round opened on production at 06:00 Berlin and emailed nobody, for two reasons.

Changing a Pulse's cadence moved a scheduled Round's open instant but kept
its planned_open_date, and opening recomputes send times from that date, so
every Invitation was scheduled a week late. One pure nextRoundSlot now picks
the date and instants for both scheduling paths, and skips skipped weeks and
dates another Round of the Pulse already holds (round is unique per date).

Sends the Organization Durable Object creates itself (Round Invitations,
send jobs, reminders, results-ready, Resend Invitation) were never put on the
Email queue. A transactional outbox (email_outbox) records each Pending send
in the same transaction and pulls the alarm to now; the alarm sends the rows
with a WriteQueue bound in the object's init phase and deletes what it sent.
delivery claims each send once, so a repeated message is harmless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

PR title: `R1 238: Round Invitations reach the Email queue, on the date the cadence names`
PR body (use exactly; pass with a heredoc, run `gh pr create` with `</dev/null`):
```
## Why
Members must get a Round's Invitation by email at the time the Pulse says. On 2026-11-18 the "Claude Test" Round opened on production at 06:00 Berlin (alarm ran, outcome ok) and nobody got an email: D1 `invitation_index` is empty for every Round, and the Round's `plannedOpenDate` was 2026-11-24 although it opened on the 18th. Fixes #238.

## What changed
- **Round date (bug 1).** `updateScheduledRoundForPulse` updated the open instant but not `planned_open_date`; `executeOpenJob` recomputes send times from the date, so Invitations went on a `send` job a week later. A pure `nextRoundSlot` (domain `Lifecycle.ts`) now gives date and instants to both `scheduleNextRound` and the update, which writes the date too. It avoids skipped weeks and every date another Round of the Pulse holds, since `round` is unique on `(pulse_id, planned_open_date)` including cancelled Rounds.
- **Outbox (bug 2).** Only Worker HTTP handlers wrote to the Email queue, so every send the Organization object created itself stayed `Pending`. `organization/EmailOutbox.ts` wraps the object's SendStore: a Pending create or a requeue inserts an `email_outbox` row in the same transaction and calls `repairAlarm`, which now targets `min(now, next job)` while rows wait. The alarm runs due jobs, sends up to 100 rows per batch through `Cloudflare.Queues.WriteQueue` (bound in the object's init phase, `WriteQueueBinding` provided on `OrganizationLive`), then deletes `id <= last sent`. A crash between send and delete repeats a message; `deliver` claims each send once.
- Worker-created sends now get a second queue message (Worker EmailOutbox plus the object's outbox). Harmless; removing the Worker side is #239.

## Verification
- `nextRoundSlot` property test (weekday, open instant ahead, instants recomputed from the date, first free date) fails on two planted bugs.
- New adapter test on local workerd moves a Pulse's cadence, runs the open job, and waits for the Invitation in `captured_email`. It fails with the outbox dispatch removed (no email) and with the old date SQL (`expected 1794988800000 to equal 1795420800000`).
- Full gate locally: typecheck, ledger, comments, format, lint, 1203 unit and 241 privacy tests. Organization.test.ts passed 4 runs in a row.
- Fixture changes: the Round lifecycle route waits for the alarm to return to the earliest job once the outbox drains; the test-Invitation route uses a per-run admin address; the Submission exchange test retries a 5xx, because local D1 throws a transient "Failed to get session commit token" under the extra consumer writes.

## Not covered
- If the Email queue is down longer than the platform's alarm retries, waiting rows sit until the next send, job, or the daily cron `repairAlarm`.
- The production Round opened today still has its Invitations on a job for 2026-11-24; this change does not rewrite it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

Verification already run by the main session: typecheck, check:ledger, check:comments, format:check, lint, pnpm test (1203 passed), pnpm test:privacy (241 passed).

Return the PR URL and the head commit SHA.

SP=/tmp/claude-1001/-home-ubuntu--t3-worktrees-surveybeat-next-t3-ce5edeb0-dc00b1e3277f51fd/24bf2097-4a23-40ae-ab7f-5e51818792bb/scratchpad && mkdir -p "$SP" && cat > "$SP/pr-238-body.md" <<'EOF'
## Why
Members must get a Round's Invitation by email at the time the Pulse says. On 2026-11-18 the "Claude Test" Round opened on production at 06:00 Berlin (alarm ran, outcome ok) and nobody got an email: D1 `invitation_index` is empty for every Round, and the Round's `plannedOpenDate` was 2026-11-24 although it opened on the 18th. Fixes #238.

## What changed
- **Round date (bug 1).** `updateScheduledRoundForPulse` updated the open instant but not `planned_open_date`; `executeOpenJob` recomputes send times from the date, so Invitations went on a `send` job a week later. A pure `nextRoundSlot` (domain `Lifecycle.ts`) now gives date and instants to both `scheduleNextRound` and the update, which writes the date too. It avoids skipped weeks and every date another Round of the Pulse holds, since `round` is unique on `(pulse_id, planned_open_date)` including cancelled Rounds.
- **Outbox (bug 2).** Only Worker HTTP handlers wrote to the Email queue, so every send the Organization object created itself stayed `Pending`. `organization/EmailOutbox.ts` wraps the object's SendStore: a Pending create or a requeue inserts an `email_outbox` row in the same transaction and calls `repairAlarm`, which now targets `min(now, next job)` while rows wait. The alarm runs due jobs, sends up to 100 rows per batch through `Cloudflare.Queues.WriteQueue` (bound in the object's init phase, `WriteQueueBinding` provided on `OrganizationLive`), then deletes `id <= last sent`. A crash between send and delete repeats a message; `deliver` claims each send once.
- Worker-created sends now get a second queue message (Worker EmailOutbox plus the object's outbox). Harmless; removing the Worker side is #239.

## Verification
- `nextRoundSlot` property test (weekday, open instant ahead, instants recomputed from the date, first free date) fails on two planted bugs.
- New adapter test on local workerd moves a Pulse's cadence, runs the open job, and waits for the Invitation in `captured_email`. It fails with the outbox dispatch removed (no email) and with the old date SQL (`expected 1794988800000 to equal 1795420800000`).
- Full gate locally: typecheck, ledger, comments, format, lint, 1203 unit and 241 privacy tests. Organization.test.ts passed 4 runs in a row.
- Fixture changes: the Round lifecycle route waits for the alarm to return to the earliest job once the outbox drains; the test-Invitation route uses a per-run admin address; the Submission exchange test retries a 5xx, because local D1 throws a transient "Failed to get session commit token" under the extra consumer writes.

## Not covered
- If the Email queue is down longer than the platform's alarm retries, waiting rows sit until the next send, job, or the daily cron `repairAlarm`.
- The production Round opened today still has its Invitations on a job for 2026-11-24; this change does not rewrite it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
PR #240 is open for `t3/round-invitation-at-6`. It was not merged.

- **Commit:** `9ff21277f80a829deb58e1d4e4fad4aa76b50257`, "R1 238: Round Invitations reach the Email queue, on the date the cadence names". It includes the 12 files you listed and nothing under `.githooks/`, which is still modified and untracked and untouched.
- **Commit path:** I used plain `git commit` with the files staged by name, not `but commit`. The fence refuses `but commit` because it skips the hooks. Before committing I ran `node scripts/fence/gate.mjs` as the fence asked, and it passed. The commit then ran the normal pre-commit hook, which also passed. Signing was not changed.
- **Push:** `git push -u origin HEAD` was rejected with "missing necessary objects". The remote branch did not exist and the remote URL was already HTTPS, so I did not retry SSH. I then pushed once over HTTPS with the gh credential helper, and it succeeded. Because that push used the URL, no upstream tracking was set, and the remote config is unchanged.
- **Pull request:** https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/pull/240
- **Head SHA:** `9ff21277f80a829deb58e1d4e4fad4aa76b50257`

The PR title and body are exactly as you gave them. The body file is at `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-ubuntu--t3-worktrees-surveybeat-next-t3-ce5edeb0-dc00b1e3277f51fd/24bf2097-4a23-40ae-ab7f-5e51818792bb/scratchpad/pr-238-body.md`. The Co-Authored-By trailer in the commit is the Opus one you specified.
